#### §22: Threads

| ID | Spec | Ann. | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|
| D-22.1 | §22.4 | ARB, COMPAT | Every sync object fits its ABI size, is valid when all-zero (static initializers), and holds no pointers, so it works process-shared and survives being moved between processes by `mmap`. |
| D-22.2 | §22.3 | HIST | **Cancellation is an explicit internal error.** Deferred cancellation makes the current cancellation point return `Error::Canceled`. That propagates through Rust frames normally, and at the ABI boundary `ret` hands it to `rt::cancel::act()`. `act()` runs the cleanup handlers and performs the forced unwind of the *caller's* frames, never unwinding a Rust frame. Asynchronous cancellation is acted on only while the thread executes outside the library's text range, and is deferred to the next boundary crossing otherwise (F12, F39). |
| D-22.3 | §22.1 | — | C11 `thrd_*`/`mtx_*`/`cnd_*`/`tss_*` are translations of the same internals. |
| D-22.4 | §22.5 | HIST | Read-write locks default to prefer-reader, per the contract. A fair policy is available internally. |
| D-22.5 | §22.6 | ARB | Keys beyond `PTHREAD_KEYS_MAX` are allowed (P-lift). The constant stays 1024 in the ABI. |
| D-22.6 | §22.6 | HIST | The static TLS surplus for initial-exec (`DF_STATIC_TLS`) `dlopen` objects is `glibc.rtld.optional_static_tls` plus 1200 bytes, 1712 bytes by default, as on the reference (D-27.94, story TLS-DYNAMIC-BLOCKS; corrected 2026-11-23: until then it was a fixed 64 KiB that the tunable did not change, and a thread stack taken from the cache zeroed all of it on every reuse). Objects without `DF_STATIC_TLS` take no surplus: their blocks are made per thread on first access (DL-19). Dynamic TLS never fails except for `ENOMEM`, which ends the process with status 127, per the contract (§27.3). |
| D-22.7 | §22.9 | KERN | The library owns the per-thread rseq registration and publishes `__rseq_*`. |
| D-22.8 | §22.10 | HIST | We ship our own `libthread_db` describing our layout (F30). |
| D-22.9 | §22.1–22.2, §22.6, §22.9 | KERN, ARB | **The thread runtime** (phase 6). `pthread_t` is the thread pointer (as glibc). One mapping per thread: guard (rounded to pages; none when 0), stack, static TLS block, thread block, then the *descriptor* (start routine and argument, result, join and detach state, cancellation word, cleanup-buffer chain, setxid request word, stack bounds, the robust-list head, the 32-byte-aligned rseq area, the key table pointer, the per-thread result slots of D-H3), whose address the thread block holds. A caller-supplied stack (`attr_setstack`) gets the TLS block, thread block and descriptor at its top. Creation is `clone3` (falling back to `clone`) with the flags of §22.1, through `machine/thread_start.S`, which switches to the new stack, calls the runtime's entry, and makes the `exit` system call if it ever returns. The kernel writes the TID into the thread block (0x84, `CLONE_PARENT_SETTID`) and clears it at exit (`CLONE_CHILD_CLEARTID`), which is the futex `join` waits on; `gettid` is that load. The main thread's TID comes from `set_tid_address` at startup. The new thread registers its robust list and rseq area itself (Liella owns rseq in its processes, D-22.7; `glibc.pthread.rseq=0` disables it) and publishes `__rseq_offset`/`__rseq_size`/`__rseq_flags`. Stacks of exited threads are cached (up to 40 MiB, glibc's figure) and reused only once their TID word is 0. **No transparent huge pages on thread mappings (owner ruling 2026-10-01).** Before Linux 6.7 a `MAP_STACK` mapping may take transparent huge pages; one that merges with an adjacent anonymous mapping can then have a fault fill a whole 2 MiB range, making the neighbour's untouched pages resident (found by `s11_10_c_10`, which a glibc thread stack did this to). So on a kernel whose `uname` release is below 6.7, each thread mapping is made `PROT_NONE`, marked `MADV_NOHUGEPAGE`, then opened, so it is never usable unmarked. 6.7 made `MAP_STACK` imply `VM_NOHUGEPAGE`, and there the mapping is made as before. Default stack size: the `RLIMIT_STACK` soft limit at startup, 2 MiB if unlimited (§22.2). A thread list (lock-protected; changed only at create and exit) serves setxid, `fork` and `pthread_getattr_np`. `__libc_single_threaded` becomes 0 at the first creation and stays 0 (P5). |
| D-22.10 | §22.1 | — | **Threads Liella did not create.** In a test process the host C library starts (D-4.15) every thread is glibc's. Liella's thread-block fields there are glibc's zero reserved area (0x80–0x280), and a reused glibc stack keeps them: such a thread inherits the `errno` slot and heap cache of the dead thread whose block it reuses. That is sound for the heap, because exactly one live thread uses a block at a time, and it is the only case: a cache of a glibc thread whose stack is unmapped is never parked (it leaks its partial slabs; test processes only). What needs the TID asks the kernel (`gettid`) instead of the thread block, because a reused block's TID word is stale; descriptor-backed operations (`join`, cancellation, setxid) are defined only for threads Liella created (`FLAG_OWN`). In a process Liella started, or under glibc's `ld.so` with Liella's `libc.so.6`, every thread is Liella's. **Interim gap (owner ruling 2026-10-01): dynamically linked programs.** Under another `ld.so`, a new thread's TLS for every loaded module must come from that loader's private interface (glibc's `_dl_allocate_tls`), which Liella does not use. Until Liella's own `ld.so` (phase 14), `pthread_create` and `thrd_create` in a dynamically linked program fail with `EAGAIN`. Statically linked programs, which Liella starts itself, have full threads. That covers the conformance suite, which links statically and suffices for this milestone. In-process tests that create Liella threads run start routines that call only Liella and atomics (the host library's TLS is not set up in them); the full contracts run as C conformance programs against the products. (Amended by D-27.36.) |
| D-22.11 | §22.3 | KERN, HIST | **Cancellation mechanics** (refines D-22.2). A cancellation point checks the descriptor's cancellation word on entry (`Err(Canceled)` if acted on) and makes its blocking system call through a C-layer *window* primitive (`liella_sys_cancellable`: check the word, then `syscall`, between two exported labels). The internal signal's handler, interrupting a thread whose program counter is inside the window (the system call had no effect: the kernel restarts it, or it has not started), rewrites the saved program counter to the primitive's cancelled exit, which returns `-ECANCELED`; the Rust caller turns that into `Err(Canceled)`, which propagates to the export (no Rust frame is skipped). Past the `syscall` instruction (a completed call, or a partial transfer) the request stays pending for the next point (§22.3 guarantees). **Asynchronous cancellation (owner ruling 2026-10-01, interim):** it takes effect only at safe points outside Liella code. The handler acts immediately only when it can prove the interrupted program counter lies outside Liella's text, from text bounds the products' link records. Where no such bounds exist, in a statically linked program until the product build marks them and in test processes, the request stays pending. It is then acted on at the thread's next safe point: a cancellation point, `pthread_testcancel`, or `pthread_setcancelstate`/`setcanceltype` (the only async-cancel-safe calls). **Known deviation from glibc,** which acts immediately at any instruction: a thread that runs only its own code with asynchronous cancellation enabled is not cancelled until it reaches such a point. This is the owner's chosen tradeoff, preferred over guessing the text boundary in a statically linked program. Revisit if coreutils' tests fail because of it. **Acting** runs the C cleanup buffers that `pthread_cleanup_push` registered (`__pthread_register_cancel`: each is a `__sigsetjmp` buffer; `__pthread_unwind_next` continues to the next), then key and `thread_local` destructors, then exits with `PTHREAD_CANCELED`. **Interim until phase 14:** glibc runs the cleanup through `_Unwind_ForcedUnwind` from `libgcc_s` (loaded by `dlopen`), which also runs C++ destructors and `-fexceptions` `__attribute__((cleanup))` handlers. Without `dlopen` (phase 14), Liella runs only the registered C buffers; a cancelled or exiting C++ thread skips its destructors. C programs (the coreutils target) are complete. **Fast points (CANCEL-FAST, 2026-10-11):** `read`, `write`, `pread`/`pread64`, `pwrite`/`pwrite64`, `__read_chk`, `__pread_chk`/`__pread64_chk` and `close`/`__close` act on a due request themselves (`sys::point4`, `sys::close_point`, `cancel::act`) instead of setting `CANCEL_HIT` for `cancel::point`; the order of effects is unchanged: `errno` from the call's result, then acting. The 4-argument calls enter the same window through `liella_machine_syscall_cancel4` (all arguments in registers, no stack arguments; the word's address moves to `%r11` before the window, so the window is still exactly load-test-`syscall` for both entries). No single-threaded special case: the window's first load IS the one-load "nothing to act on" check, in every thread. **Happens-before argument (unchanged by the fast path):** a request is published by `pthread_cancel`'s `fetch_or(REQUESTED)` (AcqRel) BEFORE it signals the thread. (a) If the target's window load comes after that RMW in the word's modification order, it reads REQUESTED and returns -ECANCELED without the system call. (b) If the load came earlier, the signal is sent after the RMW and delivered at the next kernel entry: while the program counter is between the load and the `syscall` instruction (the handler redirects it), during the system call (a restartable call is rewound to the `syscall` instruction, inside the window: redirected; a completed or partial transfer is past `window_end`: the request stays pending for the next point, as the row above says). A self-request (`pthread_cancel(pthread_self())` before the call) is sequenced before the load: case (a). `close` keeps its own order (the descriptor is closed outside the window, then the word is read: a request due then acts). No path skips the load; an interruption with -EINTR re-reads the word, as before. **Kernel ECANCELED (CANCEL-FAST-2, 2026-10-11, coordinator decision):** a point acts on a -ECANCELED (or -EINTR) result ONLY when the word says a request is due (`cancel_due`, `sys::found_due`); otherwise it is an ordinary error result (-1, errno ECANCELED), e.g. a timerfd read after a clock change or a seccomp filter. Sound because the window returns -ECANCELED only for a due request and only the thread itself can make a due request not due. Test: conformance/c/s22_cancel_fast.c part 5 (seccomp ECANCELED, main and created thread). Not changed: the futex waits of `pthread_cond_wait`/`sem_wait`/`pthread_join` (sync.rs `ThreadCtx::wait`) still read a raw -ECANCELED as acted on; futex(2) never returns ECANCELED itself (only a seccomp filter could); follow-up. **Direct points (CANCEL-FAST-2, 2026-10-11):** in the products `read`, `write`, `pread`/`pread64`, `pwrite`/`pwrite64` and `close`/`__close` are assembly entries (csys/src/machine/points.S; plan S2 hot-kernel; Rust twins `export! { asm }` call the same code in the tests). The common case: the descriptor word at `%fs:0xa0` (non-zero), count 1..=isize::MAX and a non-NULL buffer, then `call` into the SAME window (`liella_machine_cancel_window`, word address in `%r11`), then one result test; an error result tail-jumps to `liella_cancel_point_fail` (the rule above, errno, -1). Everything else tail-jumps to the former Rust export (`liella_*_rest`), unchanged. `close` makes its call first (outside any window), then reads the word: due, or an error, goes to `liella_close_point_fail`. The happens-before argument above is unchanged: the window is the same code and the first load is still its first instruction. `close` takes the Rust path (`aio::closing`) once any asynchronous I/O was started: one flag byte `liella_machine_aio_used`, set before the first request is counted (`PENDING`) or an internal descriptor is published (`RING_FD`, `EVENT_FD`), so a close that the old code would have seen as busy (its submission happened-before the close) sees the flag. |

(1) Futex wrappers thin and typed; private scope adds `FUTEX_PRIVATE_FLAG`; a deadline uses `FUTEX_WAIT_BITSET` with `FUTEX_CLOCK_REALTIME` (the only absolute wait); errors returned, callers re-check. (2) `RawMutex`: one zero-initialised `u32`, bit 0 locked, bits 1-31 the count of registered sleepers; lock CAS 0 to 1, slow path a short read-only spin, then register (+2) and wait on the exact value; unlock one `fetch_sub(1)`, wake exactly when the count was non-zero (the classic 0/1/2 design wakes needlessly). `reset` in the fork child stores 0. (3) `RawOnce`: bit 0 running, bit 1 sleepers, 4 done; an unwinding routine puts the word back to new and wakes the sleepers (POSIX `pthread_once` rule; a deliberate change, pinned by P1). (4) `RawRwLock` (D-22.4 reader-preferring): bit 0 writer, bit 1 sleepers, readers in units of 4; the unlock that frees the lock clears bit 1 and wakes all. (5) `RawCondvar`: a sequence word; `notify_all` increments then wakes all (no lost wake-up); broadcast only. (6) `cpu::Features`: a `Copy` value of the raw registers, cached once by the boundary; at most five `cpuid` (STARTUP-COST); out-of-range leaves not read; AVX family needs XCR0 bits 1-2, AVX-512 bits 1-2 and 5-7; psABI levels v2/v3/v4. (7) TLS: the thread-block layout and its offset asserts unchanged (ERRATA E7, D-22.10); initial area `A = max(64, p_align)`, thread pointer the first A-aligned address at least `tls` above the base, slack `A - PAGE` when A exceeds a page, checked arithmetic; canary = first 8 `AT_RANDOM` bytes with the low byte zeroed, pointer guard the next 8. (8) Fatal path: no allocation, lock or stdio; one `writev` per diagnostic (chunks of 16), resuming after partial writes and EINTR, giving up on other errors (P2); `abort` unblocks and raises SIGABRT, then the default disposition, then a trap, then `_exit(127)`, streams not flushed; assertion texts in the ERRATA E8 form. (P1-P2, P4) The unwind rule of `RawOnce` and the EINTR rule of `fatal::message` are new contracts with tests; four further contracts (condvar sequence, futex realtime clock, leaf-7 bound, canary bytes) got deterministic tests. |

(2) `destroy` detaches and frees the block, or leaves it to the last waiter still inside (a destroy right after a broadcast is allowed); 1000 init/use/destroy cycles leave no block. (3) No old object is process-shared: `init` with `PTHREAD_PROCESS_SHARED` (or `CLOCK_MONOTONIC`) zeroes the word and returns `EINVAL`, as glibc, so no heap pointer is ever shared between processes. | D-22.14 | §22.4 | ABI | **`__count` is kept by recursive mutexes only** (TIMING-N100-MUTEX-MT, -2, 2026-11-06). The second word of `pthread_mutex_t` (`__data.__count`) holds the recursion depth of a private recursive mutex (1 held once, n held n times, 0 free); a private normal, error-checking or adaptive mutex leaves it 0, held or free, in the fast path (`Mutex::lock_fast`/`unlock_fast_deferred`) and the general path alike. Robust, priority-inheritance, priority-protected and process-shared mutexes keep their earlier layout. Settled by a black-box probe of the reference glibc (cached hash b2d4f23094db: 0 for normal, error-checking and adaptive mutexes held or free, before and after `pthread_create`; 1 for a recursive mutex held once), so the layout matches glibc and needs no differences row. Gain: one store fewer on each uncontended lock and release of the non-recursive types, ahead of the LOCK-prefixed instruction that must drain it. The type is tested once, before the acquire, so the recursive path costs no extra instruction. Tests: `only_a_recursive_mutex_keeps_a_count`, the count-word assertion in `every_mutex_type_excludes` (crates/rt/tests/pthread_sync.rs). |

A listed thread whose tid word is 0 or whose descriptor has the exited flag is `TD_THR_ZOMBIE`. List walks stop after 2^20 entries, so a damaged list in a core file cannot hang the debugger. Agents come from a static pool of 64 (the library has no allocator). *TLS.* `td_thr_tlsbase(th, modid)` returns the module's block from the thread's dtv when the loader made one; in a static program (no dtv) module 1's block ends at the thread pointer: `tp - round_up(memsz, align)` from the TLS image record. `td_thr_tls_get_addr` (by link_map) returns `TD_NOCAPAB` until the loader publishes a link_map list. *Not offered* (`TD_NOCAPAB` / `TD_NOEVENT` / `TD_NOXREGS`): event reporting (debuggers learn of threads from ptrace clone and exit events), thread-specific data, extra register sets, suspend/resume, setting priority or signals. *Scope.* Proven on STATIC programs: gdb lists the threads, each thread's backtrace and a `__thread` variable per thread, live and from a core file (`thread_db_products.rs`). | D-22.18 | §22.5 | COMPAT | **Read-write lock calls on a lock the caller already holds** (issue #15; D-22.4). Every lock call checks in this order before it looks at the lock state: (1) a timed or clock form validates its deadline, so `tv_nsec` outside [0, 1e9) or an unknown clock is `EINVAL` whatever the lock state, even when the lock is free; (2) a lock the caller holds for writing is `EDEADLK` from `rdlock`, `wrlock` and the timed and clock forms, and `EBUSY` from `tryrdlock` and `trywrlock`, which take no self-deadlock check and report the lock busy like any lock they cannot take. POSIX requires `EBUSY` from a try-lock that cannot acquire and only allows `EDEADLK`; callers read `EBUSY` from a try-lock as "held" and treat `EDEADLK` as fatal (Berkeley DB's shared latches probe with `tryrdlock` and refuse to open an environment). POSIX also lets a timed lock skip the deadline check when the lock is free; checking it first gives one answer for a bad deadline whatever the lock state. Every cell (static initialiser, default attributes, each kind `setkind_np` accepts, private and process-shared; caller holding nothing, a read lock or the write lock; each non-blocking call form) was settled by a black-box probe of the reference and is pinned by `conformance/c/s22_rwlock_self.c`. |
| D-22.19 | §22.1, §22.3 | HIST | **`pthread_exit` and acting on cancellation unwind the thread's stack with the program's unwinder** (issue #25; ends D-22.11's interim). Designed from the Itanium C++ ABI's base unwinding interface (§1.2 `struct _Unwind_Exception`, §1.3 `_Unwind_ForcedUnwind` with a stop function, `_UA_FORCE_UNWIND`, `_UA_END_OF_STACK`) and POSIX `pthread_exit`/cancellation (cleanup handlers, then thread-specific destructors). **Where the unwinder comes from:** at each exit, `_Unwind_ForcedUnwind` and `_Unwind_GetCFA` are looked up through the loader's `dlsym` entry with `RTLD_DEFAULT` (the definitions the program's own references bind to: `libgcc_s.so.1`, which every C++ program and every `-fexceptions` C program with cleanups loads, or another unwinder the program loaded). Nothing is looked up or stored at start-up or thread creation, and nothing is cached (a `dlopen` or `dlclose` changes the answer). libniji loads no unwinder itself: a process without one (a C program that never needed one, a statically linked program) exits as before, jumping to the C cleanup buffers newest first, so it never fails for want of `libgcc_s.so.1`. **The unwind:** the exception object (class `NIJIEXIT`) lives in the thread descriptor (`UnwindArea`, 48 bytes), not on the stack the landing pads reuse. The stop function runs for each frame before its cleanups: the old-style records (`_pthread_cleanup_push`) of frames already left run, and when the newest `__pthread_register_cancel` buffer lies below the frame's canonical frame address it is jumped to; its handler calls `__pthread_unwind_next`, which starts a new unwind from there, so C buffers, `-fexceptions` cleanups and C++ destructors run in frame order. At `_UA_END_OF_STACK` (the thread's start or `_start`, which carry no return address) the remaining buffers and records run, then the exit sequence (`thread_local` and key destructors, D-22.11). If the unwind cannot start, the exit goes on without it. **A handler that does not rethrow** (C++ requires the rethrow; ruling #6884, THREAD-FORCED-UNWIND-2): the exception's cleanup function, which `__cxa_end_catch` calls at that handler's end, ends the process: `FATAL: exception not rethrown` on standard error, then `abort` (SIGABRT). The thread can neither go on (it was told to exit) nor exit from there with the frames outside the handler unwound; the black-box probe that settled this choice is reported in the THREAD-FORCED-UNWIND-2 hand-back. **Not covered:** a statically linked program (libc.a has no way to find libgcc_eh's entries without a weak reference that would also land in libc.so.6) and a program that carries its own unwinder hidden (`-static-libgcc`) keep the buffers-only exit. Cost: the lookup is two `dlsym` calls per exit through `pthread_exit` or cancellation (measured 11-20, Skylake-SP host, user-mode instructions: 3,656 per pair, of 68,518 per thread created, exited through `pthread_exit` from a C++ frame and joined; not cached, see the THREAD-FORCED-UNWIND-2 handoff); in a process without an unwinder the miss also sets the thread's `dlerror` text, made once per thread and released at its exit (DL-15). Probe (glibc 2.39, Skylake-SP host, black box): destructors run, `catch (abi::__forced_unwind &)` and `catch (...)` entered at `pthread_exit` and at each cancellation point kind, `pthread_cleanup_push` with `-fexceptions` runs in frame order with `__attribute__((cleanup))`, main thread destructors run; libniji now matches on every case. (Amended by D-22.21.) |
| D-22.20 | §22.6 | — | **The initial thread keeps the words it was given before `main` (story ASAN-MAIN-THREAD, GitHub issue #26).** Under libniji's `ld.so` the program's `.preinit_array` and every shared object's initialisation run before `__libc_start_main` takes the process for the runtime (D-27.24). Until then the C library treats the process as one it did not start (D-22.10, D-X.60), so the initial thread's per-thread words live in its registry entry: `errno`, `h_errno`, the descriptor with its key values (`pthread_setspecific`), the `uselocale` choice with its ctype and view words, the C++ `thread_local` destructor list, the heap cache, the resolver state and the cache words. `init_initial` now moves every non-zero word of that entry into the thread's own block before it marks the process as the runtime's, and reuses a descriptor made there instead of mapping a new one; a word the entry never set keeps the block's value (the loader's `flags`). Black-box probes on the reference 2.39 (Zen 1 build host, gcc 13): a key value, `errno` and a `uselocale` choice set in `.preinit_array` are seen by a library constructor and `main`, and a `thread_local` destructor registered in a library constructor runs at `exit`; libniji before this change lost all four. A sanitizer runtime records its main thread with `pthread_setspecific` from `.preinit_array`: losing it made ASan report `thread T-1` and stop on its own internal check before the allocation stack and the summary. The move is one cold function, run once at start-up; when nothing used the registry before `main` it finds no registry chunk and maps none, and `init_initial` stores the descriptor it makes straight into the thread's block. |
| D-22.21 | §22.1, §22.3 | HIST | **A static program's exiting or cancelled thread unwinds with the unwinder the program links** (amends D-22.19, which left static programs on the buffers-only exit; ruling #6885). A static program has no loader, so D-22.19's `dlsym` lookup finds nothing. `csys/src/machine/unwinder.S` gives `niji_machine_unwind_force` and `niji_machine_unwind_get_cfa`, the addresses of `_Unwind_ForcedUnwind` and `_Unwind_GetCFA` (Itanium C++ ABI §1.3) or 0. As the C layer builds it (libc.so.6, ld.so, the test binaries) both return 0. `cargo xtask so` assembles the same file with `-DNIJI_STATIC_ARCHIVE` and puts it in the published `libc.a` in place of that member: there the references are weak, so a static link that takes the compiler's unwinder (`libgcc_eh`: a C++ runtime throws through it, `-fexceptions` cleanups resume through it) resolves them, and a program that needs no unwinder (a C program without unwind cleanups) links none because of libc.a and keeps the buffers-only exit. The thread's exit asks the linked unwinder first (two calls that return a constant), then the loader's `dlsym` as in D-22.19. **Checks:** the build fails unless the replaced member is the archive's only reference to those two names and a weak one, and unless libc.so.6's dynamic symbol table names neither (no symbol, relocation or start-up lookup in the shared library). **`-static-libgcc`:** such a program's own unwinder is hidden (libgcc_eh's symbols have hidden visibility), so nothing outside the program can find it. A C++ program linked that way with the shared C++ library still loads `libgcc_s.so.1` through it, and the exit unwinds with that copy; the program's landing pads resume with their own copy (tested). A `-static-libgcc` program that loads no `libgcc_s.so.1` (C with `-fexceptions`, or C++ with `-static-libstdc++`) keeps the buffers-only exit: its C cleanup buffers and key and `thread_local` destructors run, its unwind cleanups and C++ destructors do not (open for a ruling, THREAD-FORCED-UNWIND-STATIC hand-back). **Cost:** none at start-up; in libc.a two weak references and two 3-instruction functions in a member a thread's exit already pulls; in libc.so.6 the two functions that return 0 (cold text) and one more call per thread exit. Probe (glibc 2.39, Skylake-SP host, black box): the oracle programs `forced_unwind.cc` and `forced_unwind.c` (three builds) linked `-static`, and `forced_unwind.cc` linked `-static-libgcc`, print the same text as the dynamic ones; libniji now matches on each. (Amended by D-22.23.) |
| D-22.22 | §22.4 (s22_4_c_5), §22.5, §22.7 (s22_7_c_2) | KERN | **A timed wait never retries a wait the kernel refused; a negative `tv_sec` is a passed deadline** (TIMED-WAIT-PAST-DEADLINE, 2026-11-22). Every futex wait loop (mutex plain, adaptive, priority-protected and robust; condition variable; read-write lock read and write; semaphore; timed and clock join) sorts the wait's result with `futex::woken`: woken, `EAGAIN` and `EINTR` are wake-ups (the loop re-checks its condition; the semaphore alone ends on `EINTR`, being interruptible), and every other result ends the call with that error: `ETIMEDOUT`, `ECANCELED`, or a kernel rejection (`EINVAL`, `EFAULT`, `ENOSYS` from a filter), which a retry could never get past. A deadline whose `tv_sec` is negative is before every reading of `CLOCK_REALTIME` and `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` (neither is ever negative), and the kernel rejects it with `EINVAL`: `futex::wait_until` returns `ETIMEDOUT` for it without the call, and a cancellation point waits until {0, 0} instead (also past on both clocks, so a due cancellation request is still acted on). A free object is still taken first, so such a deadline is no error when the call need not wait. The priority-inheritance mutex keeps handing its deadline to the kernel's lock call: `EINVAL` for a negative `tv_sec` while contended, as the reference reports. Settled by a black-box probe of the reference (`conformance/c/s22_past_deadline.c --probe`, 38 call forms x 7 deadlines x contended and free); before this change 108 of libniji's cells never returned. |
| D-22.23 | §22.1, §22.3 | HIST | **A thread exit that must unwind and finds no unwinder ends the process with a message** (amends D-22.21's `-static-libgcc` case, which kept the buffers-only exit for a program that loads no `libgcc_s.so.1`; rulings #7118 and #7119: failing loudly is better than silently going on). Such a program (C with `-fexceptions`, C++ with `-static-libstdc++`) carries its unwinder hidden, so at the exit D-22.21's linked entries and D-22.19's `dlsym` lookup both find nothing. Going on skipped the unwind work: `-fexceptions` cleanups and C++ destructors did not run, a mutex a `lock_guard` owned stayed locked and `std::async`'s `get()` waited forever (no `broken_promise`). **Detection:** only then, only in a program libniji's `ld.so` started (a static program with unwind work links its unwinder, D-22.21; a process another loader started, such as the in-process test runtime whose test-profile Rust frames carry LSDAs, has no lookup to find one: gate finding `s23_4_c_3_3`), and only on the exit's first step (`pthread_exit`, `thrd_exit` or acting on cancellation; not again after each cleanup buffer), the thread's stack is walked with libniji's own call-frame walker (`niji_rt::unwind`, D-2.11, the one `backtrace` uses; `unwind::handler_above`): registers captured in the checking frame, objects found through the executable, this library's image and, for any other address, the loader's own walk over the loaded objects (`crate::backtrace::frame_object`; a static program has only the first two). A frame needs an unwind when its FDE's CIE names a personality routine (`P`) and its language-specific data pointer (`L`) is not null (or cannot be read, or the CIE has no `L`: the personality still runs). libniji's own frames with a personality (`pthread_once`'s routine frame, machine/once.S; the guarded calls, machine/guard.S) do not count: each also registers an old-style cleanup record, which the exit without an unwinder runs (conformance `s22_cancel` cancels inside a `pthread_once` routine). The Itanium C++ ABI §1.3 and the LSB's `.eh_frame` augmentation define these fields. If a frame needs one, `FATAL: an exiting or cancelled thread has frames to unwind (cleanups, destructors or handlers) and no unwinder can be found; link libgcc_s dynamically (not -static-libgcc) in a program whose threads exit or are cancelled` goes to standard error, then `abort` (SIGABRT, exit status 134). Otherwise (a plain C thread: cleanup buffers and old-style records only, or nothing) the exit without an unwinder goes on as before. The walk stops at the outermost frame (no return address), an address no object describes, a row it cannot evaluate, or 65,536 frames, and answers for the frames it saw (a frame beyond such a break is not seen: the exit then goes on as before). **Cost:** nothing at start-up or thread creation; with an unwinder found (every dynamic C++ program, every program loading `libgcc_s.so.1`), nothing; without one, one walk per exit through `pthread_exit` or cancellation (not per return from the start routine). **Reference** (black box, glibc 2.39, Skylake-SP class host, `forced_unwind.c` in the `-fexceptions` and buffers builds and `forced_unwind.cc` with `-static-libgcc -static-libstdc++`): with `libgcc_s.so.1` installed each ends with SIGABRT (134) and no message; the build without `-fexceptions` and a thread with nothing to unwind exit normally; with `libgcc_s.so.1` hidden every build ends with SIGABRT after `libgcc_s.so.1 must be installed for pthread_exit to work`. libniji matches the status where there is unwind work and keeps the normal exit where there is none, also without `libgcc_s.so.1` (docs/differences-from-glibc.md). COMPAT-38 registers an option restoring the exit that skips the unwind work (registration only). (Amended by D-22.24.) |
| D-22.24 | §22.1, §22.3 | HIST | **A program linked by niji-gcc or niji-g++ unwinds an exiting or cancelled thread with the unwinder it links** (amends D-22.23 for those programs; RELEASE-SNAPSHOT-1122D finding F1, ruling #7744). niji-g++ links libstdc++ and libgcc_eh statically (the program's library search stays in the sysroot), so its copy of `_Unwind_ForcedUnwind` and `_Unwind_GetCFA` is hidden and D-22.19's `dlsym` finds none: since D-22.23 such a thread aborted with the FATAL message, whose fix (link `libgcc_s` dynamically) the wrapper offers no way to apply. **Design:** the wrapper's dynamic links add `niji-unwinder.o` (csys/start/unwinder.S, shipped in niji6-dev) and export its one function, `__niji_program_unwinder(which)` (`--export-dynamic-symbol`), which returns the address of `_Unwind_ForcedUnwind` (0) or `_Unwind_GetCFA` (1) as the program links them, through weak hidden references (0 when the program links no unwinder; a plain C program links none because of it). When the loader's lookup finds no unwinder and D-22.23's walk finds unwind work, the exit looks the entry up with the loader's `dlsym` and unwinds with it; the FATAL message stays for a program with neither. A later step (after a cleanup buffer's handler) looks it up again only when this exit already started an unwind (the exception's class word is the exit's), so a thread with nothing to unwind costs what it did. One unwinder per unwind: the program's personality routines and landing pads (`_Unwind_Resume`) use that copy, and so does the exit. **Weighed:** linking `libgcc_s.so.1` dynamically from niji-g++ needs the system directory on the program's run-time search (or a link from the sysroot), which the wrapper keeps out; loading `libgcc_s.so.1` on first need (the reference's approach) puts a second unwinder beside the program's own static copy, and the reference's own `-static-libgcc -static-libstdc++` builds end with SIGABRT under that arrangement (black box, glibc 2.39). **Cost:** nothing at start-up or thread creation; two dynamic symbols and 32 bytes of text per niji-gcc program; at an exit with unwind work and no shared unwinder, one more `dlsym`. Programs built by other drivers are unchanged (no entry: D-22.23). |
| D-22.25 | §22.1, §22.6 | ARB | **What a thread's creation and exit touch (THREAD-CREATE-COST).** (1) The key table keeps its scan bound: `pthread_key_create` raises a high-water mark (one past the highest slot it tries to claim) before it claims the slot, and the exit-time destructor scan and the key-area clear of a reused mapping read it in O(1); before, each searched all 4096 key numbers, twice per thread (about 34,800 of the 36,000 user instructions of one create + return + join on the Zen 1 host, gdb single-step attribution). The bound never shrinks; a racing create can only raise it early, which lengthens a scan and changes nothing else. (2) Under libniji's `ld.so` the static TLS area below a reused mapping's thread pointer (the initial modules' blocks, the 64 KiB surplus, the dtv) is the loader's to write: the C library clears only its own parts (thread block, descriptor, used key entries), the loader's `tls_init` writes each block in full (image and zeros to `p_memsz`) and every dtv slot up to the count it sets (a released module ID's slot reads 0), and the free surplus is written by the `dlopen` that places a block there, before any read (D-27 DL-16d's walk, under the thread-list lock a creation also holds). It saved 3,886 instructions and 64 KiB of stores per thread creation. A static program's TLS block is still cleared, then the image copied. |
| D-22.26 | §22.1, §22.4, §22.7 | ARB, COMPAT | **An invalid tv_nsec in a timed wait is an error only when the call would block** (coordinator ruling on #7554, by POSIX: the timed lock and wait functions "shall fail" with EINVAL for a tv_nsec outside 0..999999999 when the call would block, and the timeout "need not be checked" when the object can be taken at once). - Mutexes (`pthread_mutex_timedlock`/`clocklock`, `mtx_timedlock`), every kind: a free mutex, an owner-died robust one included, is taken through the kind's own try path without a look at the deadline; a held one gives EINVAL (C11: `thrd_error`) whatever tv_sec. `pthread_timedjoin_np`/`clockjoin_np`: a thread that has ended is joined; one that still runs gives EINVAL. A PI mutex's kernel try-lock reports a lock held by another thread as EAGAIN; libniji reports EBUSY. - Semaphores (`sem_timedwait`/`clockwait`) and read-write locks: EINVAL even when the object could be taken (POSIX allows the check there), as the reference does (black-box probe 2026-11-23); the semaphore keeps its value. - Difference (row in `docs/differences-from-glibc.md`, COMPAT-42 registered): a held mutex or a running thread with an invalid tv_nsec beside a negative tv_sec gives EINVAL, where the reference decides the past deadline first and reports ETIMEDOUT (`thrd_timedout`). Reason: POSIX's "shall fail" for a call that would block. Probe (`conformance/c/s22_past_deadline.c --probe`, reference glibc 2.39 vs libniji, Skylake-SP host): of the 46 cells with an invalid tv_nsec beside a negative tv_sec that differed, 22 now equal the reference (robust and PI mutexes free: 0; semaphores free: EINVAL; joins of an ended thread: 0) and 24 are the ruled EINVAL case above (plain mutex kinds and `mtx_timedlock` held, joins of a running thread). |
| D-22.27 | §22.4 | ARB | **A priority-protected mutex is locked by an unprivileged `SCHED_OTHER` thread on its first attempt** (#7555). POSIX lists one EINVAL for locking a `PTHREAD_PRIO_PROTECT` mutex: the calling thread's priority is higher than the mutex's ceiling. A `SCHED_OTHER` thread's priority (0) is never above a ceiling, which lies in `SCHED_FIFO`'s range (1..99), so libniji takes a free mutex. Black-box probe (2026-11-23, unprivileged, `RLIMIT_RTPRIO` 0, ceiling 1): the reference refuses a thread's first lock of such a mutex with EINVAL (main thread and a new thread alike, every lock form) and takes it on the next attempt; the result depends on the thread's earlier attempts, which POSIX does not allow for, so libniji does not follow it (row in `docs/differences-from-glibc.md`). No compatibility option: a program cannot use a refusal that a retry undoes, and restoring it would need per-thread history on the lock path. `conformance/c/s22_past_deadline.c` puts its 24 priority-protected cells back in the check, each locking thread making one attempt first so both libraries are compared on the deadline handling. Also `pthread_mutex_setprioceiling` now rejects a ceiling outside `SCHED_FIFO`'s range with EINVAL (POSIX: "out of range"; before, 0 and 100 were stored), the range `pthread_mutexattr_setprioceiling` already checked; the reference agrees (probe). Not changed (pre-existing, open): the ceiling of a fresh attribute, and of a PP mutex whose ceiling was never set, reads 0 in libniji and 1 (the `SCHED_FIFO` minimum) in the reference. |
| D-22.28 | §22.1, §22.3 | PERF | **The exit's own call-frame walk (D-22.23) reads the frame tables without per-frame copies or generic decoding.** Measured on a Zen 1 host (user instructions per exit, a returning thread's cost subtracted): a dynamic plain-C `pthread_exit` 57,115 -> 30,980 at depth 0, 97,321 -> 52,340 at depth 10, `pthread_cancel` at depth 3 70,106 -> 38,161; C++ exits and throws (the shared unwinder's path) and static exits unchanged. Four changes, all in `crates/rt/src/unwind.rs`: (1) a `.eh_frame_hdr` table in the encoding linkers write (signed 4-byte, header-relative) is taken once as a slice that must fit in its segment (loaded data is untrusted: a count running past it finds nothing) and its fields read straight from it, the generic per-field decode staying for the other encodings; (2) remembered rows are stored only when an instruction remembers one, not four copies of the row on every run; (3) the walk borrows the objects its caller holds and builds each row and register set in place, swapping two register buffers by reference, instead of copying an object, two rows and a register set (a few hundred bytes each) per frame; (4) the CIE parsed last is kept for the next frame of the same walk, keyed by its address (fixed while its frames are live). The table was already searched by binary search, so a per-object index (the first candidate) would not change the search order. Skipping the walk when no frame can have a handler needs a per-object "has a personality CIE" answer kept across `dlopen`/`dlclose` (this library's own `.eh_frame` has personality routines for its guards and is about 5,000 records): left to a follow-up with its own measurement. |
